chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rejected the testimony of the beggar who begs in his palm.
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Because he is not trusted regarding the testimony, and that is because if he is given, he is pleased, and if he is prevented, he becomes angry.

key_terms.السَّائِل: The beggar / The one who asks

ai.seo_question: Why is the testimony of a beggar rejected in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the juristic principle of 'Ghalabat al-Zann' (prevalence of suspicion) by rejecting the testimony of a beggar, whose primary motivation is material sustenance. This ruling highlights the Shia legal emphasis on 'Adalah' (integrity) and the potential for financial need to compromise a witness's impartiality, ensuring judicial fairness by excluding those with conflicting economic interests.
